The Italian form is cited as living in Jurist's book (Italian ed., Raffaello Cortina 2018), which is neither the deposit nor a supplement, so per the 2026-09-01 rule the English fallback applies and language=Italian is retained as the signal. TEXT: item_text is Table 2 of the study's own paper, transcribed VERBATIM including its typography and its typos -- item 4 reads 'tools i have learned' (lowercase i), item 18 'help me understand Emotions that I feel' (capital E), items 2 and 56 have no terminal period, and the curly quotes/apostrophes are the source's. Nothing was normalised. Those 60 strings were cross-checked against the ORIGINAL 76-item pool's variable labels in Greenberg et al.'s own deposit (10.1371/journal.pone.0185264.s003, an .sav that labels mas_1..mas_76 with full item text): all 60 match a pool item at >=0.93 similarity, and the three sub-0.97 cases are typos in the ORIGINAL labels, not in Table 2 ('It's important to understanding major life events have had an impact', and pool 73 which runs two items together). That is why the wording is recorded as the instrument publisher's own English rather than a rendering this study made. OPTION TEXT: neither this paper nor Greenberg et al. states the MAS anchors anywhere. The two endpoints shipped ('strongly disagree' at 1, 'strongly agree' at 7) come from a third source -- Vas et al.'s Hungarian validation (PMC12327597), 'The scale contains 60 items, each rated on a 7-point Likert scale (1 - strongly disagree - 7 strongly agree)' -- and the direction is confirmed against these data: Mas_53R 'I rarely think about the reasons behind why I am feeling a certain way' sits at 2.95 and Mas_34 'It is important for me to acknowledge my own true feelings' at 6.02, which only works if 7 = agree. resp 2-6 are left blank rather than padded with their own numbers; the instrument labels only the poles. Hence translation_source=mixed: item_text is official_instrument_english, the two anchors are third_party_english. MAPPING (paper_order, Step 5b status PARTIAL, VERDICT: PASS -- see verify_rinaldi_2021_mas.R): the IRW codes ARE the .sav's own column names (data/rinaldi_2021_mas.py melts Mas_1..Mas_61 by name, no positional step), but the WORDS come from Table 2's own 1..60 numbering, and 61 != 60, so the tie is an order inference and not a label match. Shipped alignment: Mas_1..Mas_56 -> Table 2 items 1..56, Mas_57 -> nothing, Mas_58..Mas_61 -> Table 2 items 57..60. Four checks: (a) the gap sits at Mas_57, total |dMean|+|dSD| = 0.394 against 0.904 for the next-best gap position -- the runner-up needs a 0.52 mean discrepancy where the in-body maximum is 0.20; (b) per-item agreement under the shipped mapping is mean |dM| = 0.064, max 0.202 (Mas_7), mean |dSD| = 0.030, on Table 2's N=506 against this table's N=258 CFA subsample; (c) the 15 R-suffixed codes are exactly the 15 lowest item-rest correlations and the two polarity classes are disjoint (R-suffixed -0.35..0.12, non-R 0.19..0.67), and those 15 column numbers are exactly the 15 negatively worded numbers in Table 2 -- which fixes the 1..56 block against ANY shift, since the reverse positions are not shift-invariant; (d) Table 3's 5-factor assignment of the 35 retained items reproduces, within-factor r 0.344-0.496 against cross-factor 0.063-0.121, 5/5. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED (why PARTIAL, not VERIFIED): 10 of the 1770 possible pairwise transpositions fit marginally better than the shipped mapping on the published statistics (best -0.165 against a per-pair misfit of 0.162 -- inside the N=506-vs-N=258 noise): data items 4/38, 11/38, 18/52, 18/38, 46/47, 11/52, 4/18, 6/46, 37/38, 29/51. Check (d) rejects 46/47 and 6/46 and both 11-pairs; the remaining six are non-reverse items dropped from the 35-item solution, which no published number separates. Mas_57 IS NOT RECOVERABLE: it is not a duplicate (its highest correlate is Mas_58 at r=0.71, ordinary for this scale), and the 16 items of the original 76-item pool that the final 60 dropped are mostly other-focused ('I try to understand the complexity of other people's emotions'), of which two are self-focused and content-plausible (pool 7 'I am aware of the emotions I feel most frequently', pool 58 'I know what environmental triggers will evoke certain emotions in me (such as anger)'). Nothing distinguishes them, so the row ships with item_text blank rather than a guess. STEP 3b (instrument match, clean): the dictionary Description already says 'MAS, 61 items, the paper's focal instrument, Italian validation, N=258' and that is what the live data is -- 61 items on 1-7, N=258, matching the CFA subsample; the ERQ/TIPI/SWLS/RFQ/GSE administered alongside are present in the .sav only as precomputed subscale totals, never as items, so there is no rival instrument this table could be. RIGHTS: no restriction locatable and nothing written to instrument_rights_register.csv, which has no MAS row. The MAS was published by its own developers in PLOS ONE under CC BY 4.0 with all 76 candidate items in the deposited .sav's variable labels, and Greenberg (the developer) is a co-author of this Italian validation, also CC BY 4.0. No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was found on any MAS page; silence is permission, so this extracts normally. FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: (i) a pending_index_notes.csv row is owed for the Mas_57 gap (status note_only) -- not written here because that file is shared with the other agents in this round; (ii) no register row is owed, and per the 2026-09-10 rule a round may not write a 'ship' row anyway. RETRY TEST: N/A for the table as a whole (clean pass). For the single blank item Mas_57 the answer is NO -- a determinate verdict: the study published stats and wording for 60 items and deposited 61 columns, and neither the paper, its correction (10.1371/journal.pone.0257989, which touches only the abstract and Fig 1), the deposit, nor the original MAS paper names the 61st. It would take the authors' own questionnaire form to resolve.

The two Q2_ codes are the source file's own prefixed names for Table 3's repeat administration of SA1 and US1. VERIFIED ANYWAY (verify_rodriguezandres_2016_mnemocity_usability.R, VERDICT: PASS): (A) article Table 10 publishes M+-SD for US1, US2, SA1-SA4 split by which interaction the child played first, which is live as cov_interaction_type (NUI n=79, gamepad n=80 here vs the paper's 72/67 -- the paper's totals are its 139-child 3D-perceiving subsample, but the whole-sample split reproduces its cells best). All 24 published cells reproduce with mean |published-observed| = 0.0274 (e.g. US1 group A 4.04 pub / 4.03 obs, group B 4.25 / 4.26; US2 4.73 / 4.72 and 4.65 / 4.64; SA3 3.89 / 3.94 and 4.04 / 4.09), and scoring all 720 permutations of the six codes puts the shipped assignment first as the strict minimum with the runner-up (the US2<->SA1 swap) at 0.0422, 1.5x worse. That margin is modest, so the script also prints the cells that separate that specific pair: the group-B SD published for US2 is 0.73 against an observed 0.73 for US2 and 0.56 for SA1. (B) The article body states 'there was a question (Q3D) about the depth perception. The question had a high score 3.6 (1-5 scale)'; the live Q3D mean is 3.69. (C) The two repeated items were separated from each other by retest correlation with their Q1 counterparts over the 159 respondents who answered all four: Q2_US1~US1 (ease~ease) r=+0.249 against Q2_US1~SA1 r=+0.010, and Q2_SA1~SA1 (fun~fun) r=+0.190 against Q2_SA1~US1 r=+0.171, so the shipped assignment sums to +0.440 against +0.181 under the swap (2.4x); the mean levels agree too (US1 4.14 -> Q2_US1 3.92, SA1 4.69 -> Q2_SA1 4.64). That is the weakest of the three links and the primary tie for those two remains Table 3's own row labels. Anchors transcribed from the bracketed Value lists with the leading '1.'/'2.' numerals stripped. OCR CAVEAT: the wording came off table images and has not been checked against any text rendering, because none exists -- worth a human spot-check. SA1 ANOMALY: Table 2 prints SA1 as 'How much fun did you have?' with an agreement scale ('1. Strongly disagree / 2.Disagree / 3.Neither agree nor disagree / 4.Agree / 5.Strongly agree'), while Table 3 prints the identical question with a fun scale ('1.Very boring / 2.Boring / 3.Regular / 4.Fun / 5.Very fun'). The agreement anchors do not fit the question and are very likely a copy-paste error in the source's Table 2 (three neighbouring rows carry that same list), but they are shipped as printed rather than silently corrected to Table 3's; flagged in public_note. Q2_SA1 carries Table 3's fun scale, which is what Table 3 prints for it. LANGUAGE: the sample is 160 Spanish children aged 5-10 tested under a Universitat Politecnica de Valencia ethics approval, so the questionnaires were administered in Spanish; the article never states this outright and no Spanish wording exists anywhere in the record -- the article XML and the single supplement (S1 File .xlsx, the only supporting information the article has) carry no questionnaire text at all beyond the English of Tables 2/3/10. So the authors' own English ships in the base fields with language=Spanish and the _translated columns omitted, per the 2026-09-01 fallback (text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied). The Spanish label is an inference from the sample and the site, not a statement in the paper. INSTRUCTIONS / SECTIONS: instructions blank -- no participant-facing instruction text is published; the article's procedure prose ('When the users had finished playing the task for the first time, they had to fill out the Q1 questionnaire') is narrative about administration, not text a child read, and was not invented into instructions or section_prompt. section_id is the single trivial value: Q1 vs Q2 is a real administration grouping but has no shared prompt text, and the codes carry the distinction themselves via the Q2_ prefix. correct_response blank -- no correct answers. RESPONSES: all five levels emitted for every item even where the live data show fewer (SA1 spans only 3-5 and SA4 only 2-5 across 159 respondents); the instrument offered all five, so the unused levels are non-endorsement, not a gap. RIGHTS: no block. The questionnaire is the authors' own ad hoc 7-question usability/satisfaction survey, not a named published instrument -- no source scale is cited for it anywhere in the article -- and instrument_rights_register.csv (59 rows) has no matching row (searched 'usability', 'satisfaction', 'mnemo', 'game'; the SWLS row is a different instrument). The wording is published by the authors themselves in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is quotable for it, so 'silence is permission' (irw#1945) applies. No register row written. STEP 3b: matches. The 9 live items on resp 1-5 are exactly the S1 File's Likert survey columns; the article's other measures (Direct/Inverse CBTT scores, MnemoCity score, and the PRE1/PRE2 two-option interaction-preference questions of Table 3) are excluded by the processing script and none appear here, so the table is the survey it is named for. One wrinkle worth recording rather than correcting: Q3D is a depth-perception/immersion question, not a usability or satisfaction item, so the table name and the dictionary Description ('usability/satisfaction survey ... 9 items') slightly over-cover it; the Description's counts are otherwise right and no dictionary correction is logged.
